title: 9 Best Looker Studio Alternatives & Competitors In 2026
summary: Looker Studio is Data Studio again since April 2026. Compare 9 alternatives, from Looker, Power BI and Tableau to Metabase and GetDot, with prices.
body_markdown:
## Looker Studio is now Data Studio: what changed in April 2026


On April 10, 2026, Google announced it was "reintroducing a beloved and familiar name, Data Studio (formerly Looker Studio)" ([Google Cloud blog](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/looker-studio-is-data-studio) ). The product had been called Looker Studio since 2022. What changed:


- **Nothing to migrate.** Google says all existing reports, data sources, assets and users move to the new experience with no action on your part.
- **Two editions.** Data Studio stays free for individual analysis and ad-hoc reports. Data Studio Pro adds AI features, Google Cloud support and enterprise security such as customer-managed encryption keys ([Data Studio](https://cloud.google.com/data-studio) ).
- **A wider job.** Data Studio is now also the place to browse Google Data Cloud assets: reports, data apps built in Colab notebooks, and conversational agents built in BigQuery.
- **A clearer split from Looker.** Google positions Data Studio for ad-hoc, personal exploration and Looker for "trusted, governed data powered by a central semantic model".


So Google Data Studio alternatives and Looker Studio alternatives are the same search. If you meant Looker, the enterprise platform, see our[Looker alternatives](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-alternatives) guide.


## Before you switch: what Data Studio already covers


Data Studio is free for creators and report viewers, and it connects to more than 1,400 data sources, including Google Sheets, Google Ads, BigQuery and Google Analytics, through prebuilt and community connectors ([Data Studio](https://cloud.google.com/data-studio) ). For a marketing team reporting on Google data, that's hard to beat on price. Two things often get missed:


- **Free reports aren't free queries.** A Data Studio report on BigQuery runs BigQuery queries. On-demand pricing is $6.25 per TiB scanned (Iowa region), with the first 1 TiB a month free ([BigQuery pricing](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/pricing) ), so a busy dashboard over large tables has a real query cost.
- **Google's AI is arriving through BigQuery.** Technical users can build conversational agents in BigQuery and share them with business users, who chat with them inside Data Studio ([Data Studio](https://cloud.google.com/data-studio) ). If your data is already in BigQuery, try that before you buy a new tool; our[BigQuery MCP and AI guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/bigquery-mcp-server) covers how they work and what they cost.


The real reasons to leave are usually structural: you need one governed definition of each metric, your company standardizes on Microsoft, your analysts need more visual depth, or people want answers rather than another report.


## The 9 best Looker Studio (Data Studio) alternatives in 2026


### 1. GetDot: ask questions instead of building reports


**Best for:** teams whose data is already in BigQuery (or another warehouse) and whose bottleneck is the queue of questions in front of the data team, not the lack of a dashboard.


GetDot (Dot, that's us) is an AI data analyst. Anyone asks questions in Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, the web app or an MCP client such as Claude; Dot writes and runs the SQL in your warehouse and answers with a chart, a written explanation and the query behind every number, and can send scheduled reviews that explain what changed. With Google data, it connects to[BigQuery](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/bigquery) with a read-only service account and reads nested GA4 export fields as they are, reads[Google Sheets](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/google-sheets) shared by link, and answers through your LookML if you also run[Looker](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/looker) . Its direct GA4 and Google Ads connectors are in beta, so for production reporting I'd point Dot at the BigQuery export instead.


**Pricing (October 2026):** Free with 300 one-time credits and full Pro features; Pro $180/month billed annually ($200 month-to-month); Team $720/month billed annually ($800 month-to-month); Enterprise custom. Every plan has unlimited users and bills on credits, not seats ([GetDot pricing](https://www.getdot.ai/pricing) ).


**Limits:** not a report designer in the Data Studio sense: it can turn an answer or a description into a published dashboard (Apps), but there's no pixel-level canvas. It works best with a warehouse or database behind it. If your reports sit on BigQuery,[try Dot on the free plan](https://app.getdot.ai/register) with the questions your dashboards were built to answer.


### 2. Looker: governed metrics on Google Cloud


**Best for:** data teams that have outgrown ad-hoc reports and want one governed set of metrics on BigQuery or another cloud warehouse.


Looker is the enterprise platform that Data Studio is now separate from. Its semantic layer, LookML, defines each metric once above your warehouse, and dashboards, embedded apps, Conversational Analytics and MCP-connected tools all draw on it ([Looker](https://cloud.google.com/looker) ). Its AI features and their costs are in our[Looker AI guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-ai) , and[Gemini in Looker vs Dot](https://www.getdot.ai/compare/looker-vs-dot) compares it with our product.


**Pricing (October 2026):** a platform fee plus Developer, Standard and Viewer licenses, on one-, two- or three-year annual commitments; Standard, Enterprise and Embed editions are all listed as "call sales" ([Looker pricing](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) ). Our[Looker pricing breakdown](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-pricing) covers what third parties report it costs.


**Limits:** no published price; the Standard edition is for teams under 50 users; someone has to learn and maintain LookML.


### 3. Microsoft Power BI: full BI at a published price


**Best for:** companies on Microsoft 365 that want governed semantic models, interactive reports and sharing through Teams, Excel, PowerPoint and SharePoint.


Power BI's public, low price makes it the easiest paid step up from a free tool: build in the free Power BI Desktop, publish with a Pro license, and share across Microsoft 365 ([Power BI](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi) ). Its Copilot needs a paid Fabric capacity of F2 or above, or Premium P1 ([Microsoft Fabric blog](https://blog.fabric.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/copilot-and-ai-capabilities-now-accessible-to-all-paid-skus-in-microsoft-fabric) ); see our[Power BI Copilot guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/power-bi-copilot) .


**Pricing (October 2026):** Free for personal use (sharing requires Pro or Premium); Pro $14 per user/month and Premium Per User $24 per user/month, both paid yearly; Embedded and Fabric capacity priced separately ([Power BI pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ). More in our[Power BI pricing guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/microsoft-power-bi-pricing) .


**Limits:** every viewer needs a Pro seat below F64 or P1 capacity, and it fits best in a Microsoft shop. If you're torn between Google and Microsoft, see[Looker vs Power BI](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-vs-power-bi) .


### 4. Tableau Cloud: deeper visual analysis


**Best for:** analysts who want drag-and-drop visual exploration and polished, presentation-ready dashboards.


Tableau, owned by Salesforce, is the classic choice when visual analysis is the work itself, at per-seat prices well above Power BI's.


**Pricing (October 2026, billed annually):** Standard edition at $75 per Creator, $42 per Explorer and $15 per Viewer per month; Enterprise at $115, $70 and $35. Higher bundles (Tableau Cloud+, Tableau+) are quoted by sales ([Tableau pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing) ). Our[Tableau pricing guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/tableau-pricing) works through team sizes.


**Limits:** role-based seats add up fast for large audiences. See[Looker vs Tableau](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-vs-tableau) if Looker is also on your list.


### 5. Tableau Next: agentic analytics on Salesforce


**Best for:** companies that run on Salesforce and Slack and want AI agents rather than dashboards as the main interface.


Tableau Next is priced separately from Tableau Cloud and sold through Salesforce as well as Tableau, including Tableau Agent, Tableau Semantics (a semantic layer) and native Slack integration. Our Tableau AI guide explains how it relates to Tableau Cloud's AI.


**Pricing (October 2026):** from $40 per user/month, billed annually ([Tableau Next pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/next) ).


**Limits:** if your data and your people live in Google Workspace and BigQuery, it's a long way from home. Our[Tableau Next vs Dot comparison](https://www.getdot.ai/compare/tableau-vs-dot) goes into the details.


### 6. Data Studio Pro (formerly Looker Studio Pro): stay and upgrade


**Best for:** teams that like Data Studio but need shared ownership of content and admin controls.


Data Studio Pro adds team content management, expanded administration and Google Cloud support to the free product; pair it with BigQuery agents for a natural-language way in.


**Pricing (October 2026):** $9 per user per project per month for a project subscription; Google notes the per-user price varies with subscription length. Pro licenses are bought from the Google Cloud console or the Google Workspace Admin Console ([Data Studio pricing](https://cloud.google.com/data-studio) ).


**Limits:** it's still a reporting tool without a central semantic model; Google itself points governed, company-wide metrics to Looker.


### 7. Metabase: open-source BI you can self-host


**Best for:** teams that want a free, open-source reporting tool on BigQuery, Postgres or another database.


Non-technical users build questions with Metabase's visual query builder, analysts switch to SQL, and both publish to shared dashboards, self-hosted or in Metabase's cloud.


**Pricing (October 2026):** Open Source is free to self-host. Metabase Cloud Starter is $100 a month including 5 users ($6 per extra user), and Pro is $575 a month including 10 users ($12 per extra user), on monthly billing; Pro adds SSO and row- and column-level permissions, and Enterprise is quoted ([Metabase pricing](https://www.metabase.com/pricing) ,[Coefficient](https://coefficient.io/metabase-pricing) ).


**Limits:** self-hosting means you run upgrades, backups and security yourself. If you keep Metabase, Dot[connects to it](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/metabase) too.


### 8. Preset (Apache Superset): open-source dashboards, hosted


**Best for:** data teams comfortable with SQL who want open-source dashboards without being tied to one vendor.


Apache Superset is an open-source BI platform under the Apache 2.0 license, with a SQL editor and a no-code chart builder ([Apache Superset on GitHub](https://github.com/apache/superset) ). Preset runs Superset as a managed cloud service ([Preset pricing](https://preset.io/pricing/) ).


**Pricing (October 2026):** Superset is free to self-host. Preset's Starter plan is free for up to 5 users, Professional is $25 per user a month on monthly billing, and Enterprise is quoted ([Preset pricing](https://preset.io/pricing/) ).


**Limits:** it suits people who write SQL more than people who drag and drop; a self-hosted Superset is yours to run and secure.


### 9. Zoho Analytics: low-cost paid BI


**Best for:** small and mid-sized businesses that want a paid BI tool with a low entry price, especially if they already run on Zoho apps.


Zoho's self-service BI tool connects to databases, files and business apps and builds dashboards and reports on top ([Zoho Analytics pricing](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/pricing.html) ).


**Pricing (October 2026):** a free plan covers small reporting needs, and paid plans start at $30 a month for Basic on monthly billing; Zoho says yearly billing is 20% cheaper ([Zoho help: pricing and payments](https://help.zoho.com/portal/en/kb/analytics/administrative-guide/subscriptions/articles/pricing-and-payments) ,[Coefficient](https://coefficient.io/zoho-analytics-pricing) ).


**Limits:** each plan caps users and rows, so the price climbs as your data and team grow.


## Other tools people compare


Our[Looker alternatives guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-alternatives) covers warehouse-native BI tools such as Omni, Sigma and Holistics, and our[Power BI alternatives](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/microsoft-power-bi-alternatives) and[Tableau alternatives](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/tableau-alternatives) guides cover the rest of the BI field. I've kept this list to tools whose prices I could check: all prices and product names here were checked on October 29, 2026, and third-party listings sometimes show older prices.
